title: Revel Bikes Announces the Ranger Ti
content:
Revel Bikes today released the Ranger Ti, the company’s first production full suspension frame built around a titanium front triangle. The frame pairs this new front end with the carbon rear triangle and links from the Ranger V3 while maintaining the same geometry and kinematics.

Titanium has been a part of Revel since before its inception. The founding team launched Why Cycles in 2016 to build modern titanium bikes. Why merged with Revel in 2023, and the titanium program has run continuously since, producing hardtails, gravel bikes, and most recently the El Jefe Grande. Revel showed their Project RaTical under their Concept Labs umbrella last summer, in their first public showing of their experimentation with 3D printing and titanium full suspension. The Ranger Ti is the culmination of all those efforts and is their first production titanium full suspension platform.

Geometry and kinematics carry straight over from the carbon Ranger V3. Higher anti-squat and higher progression keep the Ranger’s downcountry intent intact: efficient pedaling, active suspension, and a supportive, bottomless feel through the travel. A steep seat tube angle, slightly longer reach, slack head angle, and lower bottom bracket round out a geometry built for long days and confident descents.

Revel Ranger Ti Quick Hits

  • Shared geometry and kinematics with Ranger V3 Carbon
  • Shared carbon rear triangle and links
  • Four bottle/utility mounts on sizes M through XL, three on S
  • Long dropper post insertion
  • Custom rubber chainstay protection
  • Debris fender
  • UDH compatible
  • Full internal cable routing
  • Frame weight: 8.02lbs size Large (3.64kg)
  • Complete bike as shown: 29.5lb size Large (13.38kg)

Why 3D printed Titanium?

Revel used the most advanced 3D printing technology for the headtube, upper shock mount, bottom bracket, and pivot interfaces on the front triangle. This has allowed Revel to leverage the shape not only for aesthetics, but also to accomplish things traditional machining and forging cannot. Welding titanium and putting multiple pivot points in precise locations can be super tough, and create either a bike that is too heavy, not strong enough, or sacrifces on the kinematics because pivot points had construction limitations. 3D printing removes that, and allows Revel to use its “carbon engineering oversight” to make a titanium bike with all the modern features of a carbon frame. Stiff 3D printed junctions are sleeved and then welded to titanium tubing to optimize the supple ride feel of titanium and strength of 3D printing. The frames are third party ISO tested in California and represent true limits of materials engineering, 3D printing, and titanium fabrication. All combining with Revel’s carbon expertise and pivot hardware/bearing interface to make a bike that rides incredibly well.

Pricing and Availability

The first batch of Ranger Ti frames is limited to 10 pieces, individually numbered, and available for reservation now, with an expected ship date before the end of the year.

Framesets are priced at $5,969 at revelbikes.com and £4999 at revelbikes.uk

Complete builds are also available.
